name: Security Headers
what: A free scanner that reads the HTTP response headers of a public website and grades how well it uses browser security headers such as CSP, HSTS and X-Frame-Options.
when: When you launch or change a public website or web app, or after a CDN or proxy change that might strip headers.
cost_note: The website scan is free; an API is offered separately with API keys.
example: Enter the full URL of the page, for example `https://www.contoso.com`.
Review the missing headers listed in red and the raw headers the server returned.
Add the missing headers at the web server, app or CDN, starting with HSTS and a report-only Content-Security-Policy.
Scan again and compare the grade and the raw header list.
pitfalls: A strict Content-Security-Policy can break scripts; roll it out in report-only mode first.
Headers can differ between pages and redirects; test the pages users actually land on.
Some header recommendations change over time; read the explanation for each header rather than chasing the letter grade.
